mechanism_narrative: The continuing decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES implies weak commuting and footfall recovery; that suppresses discretionary trips and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is around -69% and WORKPLACES around -38% at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay near current levels or improve, but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and drifts lower, households are spending slightly more time away from home and reallocating trips toward consumer errands, which should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point week-on-week from its current level
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 22.3 to 20.0 while RETAIL_REC improved from -48.7 to -41.3 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days, or if RETAIL_REC continues falling despite lower RESIDENTIAL, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates more local, non-work trips and neighborhood circulation; that traffic spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -11.6 to -5.0 and PARKS from -31.6 to -16.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS keep improving but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week average for the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in TRANSIT above the recent trough signals eased access constraints and fewer mobility frictions; once TRANSIT stops hovering near -70%, retail visits should rebound within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -65% from baseline after being below -68% in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved modestly from -72.1 to -69.0 while RETAIL_REC improved from -48.7 to -41.3
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above -65% and RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising PARKS mobility reflects better weather or leisure-demand seasonality that usually spills into shopping and dining trips, producing a higher RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -31.6 to -16.9 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to rise but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain deeply depressed, people anchor routines at home and delay discretionary outings; this joint drag keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed below -37% and TRANSIT below -69% in all four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near current lows but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The mechanism activates only after commuting mobility recovers enough to rebuild weekday activity: once WORKPLACES improves by at least 5 points from its current level, retail demand follows within two weeks.

failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by 5 points and RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.
